 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- for the death of one Krishna Jeerao in a road traffic accident dated 25.08.2022.
2.

The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, On 25.08.2022 at about 06.00pm the deceased was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-K-3159 on the Puttaiahnapalya Circle, near Halashettihalli,
Magadi Taluk, Ramangara, a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EY-9036 came with high speed,
ridden by rider in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed against the deceased's motorcycle.
As a result of it deceased was thrown out, fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately Krishna Jeerao was shifted to the Government Hospital, Magadi, provided first aid treatment and thereafter shifted to BGS Hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as an inpatient.
In spite of best efforts by the Doctors the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
The Post Mortem was conducted at Raja Rajeshwari Medical College and Hospital, Mysore Road, Bengaluru and the body was handed over to the petitioners.

entities.text: Raja Rajeshwari Medical College and Hospital, Mysore Road
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: They performed funeral and obsequies at their native place by spending Rs.1,00,000/-.
3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, prior to the date of accident the deceased Krishna Jeerao was hale and healthy, working as Cattle Farmer and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
Now due to sudden accidental death his family put to great hardship and loss of dependency, love and affection.
The Magadi Police have registered a case against the rider of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.264/2022 p/u/Sec.279 and 304-A of IPC.
The 1 st respondent being the insurer and the 2nd respondent being the RC owner of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondent No.1 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons respondent No.2 did not appear and hence, placed ex-parte.

sentences.text:
The objections of the Respondent No.1:
It has denied all the petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EY-9036.
Further contended that as on the date of accident, the deceased did not have a valid DL and without wearing helmet rode his motorcycle.
The offending motorcycle did not have a valid FC and also the rider did not have a valid DL as on the date of accident.
The accident caused due to the rash and negligent riding by the deceased.
It has stated that the petition is not maintainable for non- compliance of Sec.134(C) & 158(6) of MV Act.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Krishna Jeerao?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.Krishna Jeero died on account of road traffic accident which took place at Puttaiahnapalya Circle, near Halashettihalli,
Magadi Taluk, Ramangara, due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06- EY-9036?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
4. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined 1st petitioner as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.15.
On the other side the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any document.

8. Heard both Counsels and perused the materials on record.
9.

My finding to the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No.1: In the affirmative Issue Nos.2 & 3: In the affirmative, Issue No.4: As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

3

sentences.text: In order to prove that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and has reiterated about the relationship in her affidavit in chief.
In addition she got marked Notarized copy of Aadhar cards of the deceased and the petitioners as per Exs.P.14 & 15.
According to Exs.P.14 the Aadhar card of the petitioner Nos.1 & 3 show the husband's and father's name as Krishna Jeerao.
In the Aadhar Card of the deceased his father's name is shown as Gango Jeerao which can also be seen in the Inquest report.
In the Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.1 at Ex.P.15, her Mother's name is shown as Narasu Bai.
But in the Inquest petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased has given statement that she has Two daughters namely 1st daughter Ashwini Bai and 2nd daughter Gayithri Bai who are the petitioner Nos.2 & 3.
Therefore, the Tribunal holds that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-

The Petitioners, to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle have examined First Petitioner/Wife of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 9.

During the cross examination of PW.1,
nothing worthwhile is elicited.
12. The accident occurred on 25.08.2022 and the FIR at Ex.P.1 was registered next day of the accident i.e., on 26.08.2022 on the complaint of one Mr. Shivajirao cousin of the deceased.
Ex.P.2 spot and seizure mahazar show the accident place and the details of the offending vehicle and the offending vehicle was seized on the same day between 9am to 10am.

The sketch at Ex.P.3 shows that the deceased was proceeding towards Puttenapalya and the offending motorcycle was going towards Lingadevarapalya, while proceeding so dashed to the deceased's motorcycle and the accident was caused in the middle of the four way circle.

Inquest Mahazar at Ex.P.5 shows the details of the deceased family and the detail about the manner of accident, witnesses to the accident etc., Ex.P.6 PM report shows that the deceased died due to Head injury sustained in a Road Traffic Accident.
The police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.7.
The respondents have not led any evidence to show the negligence on the part of the deceased.
On perusal of all the documents on records, this Tribunal holds that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No. 3:-
The petitioners have proved that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased.
There is nothing elicited by the respondent No.1 during the cross examination of PW.1 to show that they were not dependents of the deceased.
The petitioners averred that the deceased was doing Cattle Farming and getting income of Rs.40,000/- per month.

In this regard the petitioners have produced Bank Statement at Ex.P.13 it shows that the income of the petitioner varies Roopabai vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194244337/
4 from month to month.

entities.text: Roopabai vs United India Ins Co Ltd

sentences.text: As per Ex.P.13 even if we consider the average monthly income the petitioner has received from his Milk Vending from January 2022 to till August 2022, it comes to Rs.31,000/- per month.
Hence this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.31,000/- per month.
Age of the deceased 14.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.14.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
As per said document, deceased born in the year 1983 and the accident occurred on 25.08.2022.
As such, the age of the deceased is 39 years as on the date of accident.
i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased comes in 40-50 years age slab, 25% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.
Therefore, Rs.7,750/- future prospectus is to be added to his monthly income, then it comes to Rs.38,750/-.
As per Principles laid down in the case of Sarala Verma the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 15.
The deceased has a wife and 2 children.
They are all dependents of the deceased.

Since there are Three dependents then 1/3rd of the income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.25,834/- (Rs.38,750/- -
Rs.12,916/-).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.46,50,120/- (Rs.25,834/- X 12 x 15 = Rs.46,50,120/-).

ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to her family.

With respect to a spouse,
it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

15. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
16.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 36 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.

Similarly,
the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the children of the deceased, they have lost their loving,
care taking father.

Therefore, they are also entitled to Rs.44,000/-
Roopabai vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194244337/
5 each, in total Rs.1,32,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of consortium.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:-
PW.1/Petitioner has stated that she has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation and funeral expenses and obsequies etc.
In this regard the petitioners have not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.

Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.

iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:-
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.31,000/- per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/3 rd of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
v) MEDICAL EXPENSES:-
PW.1/Petitioner has stated that she has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards Medical Expenses.
In this regard the petitioners have produced medical bills at Ex.P.10 for a sum of Rs.1,08,574/-.
There is no contrary documents to these bills from the respondent No.1.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.1,08,574/- under this head.
As such, in total, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.49,30,694/-.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.49,31,000/-.
LIABILITY 17.
The respondents have failed to prove their defence by leading evidence.

Therefore,
the respondents No.1 & 2 being the Insurer and the Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the Petitioners and satisfy the award.
The respondent No.1 is directed to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Though the Petitioners claimed compensation of Rs.60,00,000, Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.49,31,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum.

Therefore,
the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is in the affirmative.

18. Issue No.4:-

6 For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.49,31,000/- (Rupees Forty Nine Lakhs and Thirty One Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the Respondent No.1 being the in- surer is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.

On deposit of the award amount and interest, Rs.10,00,000/- each shall be deposited in the name of the Petitioner Nos.1 to 3 in any bank for a period of 3 years and till petitioner No.3 attains majority and the remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of e-payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

There is no contrary documents to these bills from the respondent No.1.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.1,08,574/- under this head.
As such, in total, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.49,30,694/-.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.49,31,000/-.
LIABILITY 17.
The respondents have failed to prove their defence by leading evidence.

Therefore,
the respondents No.1 & 2 being the Insurer and the Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the Petitioners and satisfy the award.
The respondent No.1 is directed to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Though the Petitioners claimed compensation of Rs.60,00,000, Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.49,31,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum.

Therefore,
the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is in the affirmative.

6 For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.49,31,000/- (Rupees Forty Nine Lakhs and Thirty One Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the Respondent No.1 being the in- surer is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.

On deposit of the award amount and interest, Rs.10,00,000/- each shall be deposited in the name of the Petitioner Nos.1 to 3 in any bank for a period of 3 years and till petitioner No.3 attains majority and the remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of e-payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
